title: Dental Care
goal: Describe a dental concern, understand examination language, and ask about a proposed treatment.

runs.text: Toothache
means tooth pain. A
cavity
is an area of decay in a tooth. A
filling
repairs a tooth with a material; a
crown
covers a tooth.
Braces
are devices used in orthodontic treatment.
Plaque
is a film that collects on teeth. A
hygienist
provides dental hygiene care. You can use these terms to ask about care without deciding the treatment yourself.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: I have pain in a tooth on the lower left.

turns.en: I have pain in a tooth on the lower left.

runs.text: When did it start?

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: Yesterday. It hurts when I chew.

turns.en: Yesterday. It hurts when I chew.

runs.text: Have you noticed anything else?

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: A filling seems to have come out. I'm not sure.

turns.en: A filling seems to have come out. I'm not sure.

runs.text: Let's examine it.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: Could you tell me what you're looking for?

turns.en: Could you tell me what you're looking for?

runs.text: Other reports: “My crown feels loose.” “My gums bleed when I brush.” “I've noticed a sensitive area.”
Gums
are the tissue around the teeth;
sensitive
can describe an area that reacts painfully to a stimulus. “I think…” signals uncertainty, not a diagnosis.
A child-related report could be “My child's first teeth are coming in.” A cosmetic request could be “I'd like to discuss whitening.”
Whitening
changes tooth color; asking about it is not a treatment recommendation. “Can we talk about braces?” opens a separate discussion.
Please open a little wider.
Like this?

turns.speaker: Dentist

runs.text: Yes. Let me know if it hurts.

turns.en: Yes. Let me know if it hurts.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: Can we agree on a signal if I need you to stop?

turns.en: Can we agree on a signal if I need you to stop?

turns.speaker: Dentist

runs.text: Yes. Let's agree on that before we begin.

turns.en: Yes. Let's agree on that before we begin.

runs.text: Rinse
means wash an area with liquid;
brush
and
floss
name different cleaning actions. Ask your dentist about the technique: “Could you show me the technique you're recommending?” This language lesson does not prescribe a routine or a technique.
If you cannot easily speak during treatment, an agreed signal can help communicate. The example is a request for an arrangement, not a claim that a particular gesture is always recognized.

turns.speaker: Dentist

runs.text: I'd like to discuss a possible filling.

turns.en: I'd like to discuss a possible filling.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: What did you find, and what are my options?

turns.en: What did you find, and what are my options?

turns.speaker: Dentist

runs.text: I'll explain the findings and alternatives.

turns.en: I'll explain the findings and alternatives.

turns.speaker: Patient

runs.text: What would the treatment involve? Could you explain the cost too?

turns.en: What would the treatment involve? Could you explain the cost too?

turns.speaker: Dentist

runs.text: We'll go through the plan before you decide.

turns.en: We'll go through the plan before you decide.

runs.text: Extraction / removing a tooth

names a procedure. Hearing the term does not mean you must infer it is necessary. “Do I need that treatment now?” asks about timing. “I'd like to understand the alternatives first” expresses a limit. “I'm nervous about pain” states a real concern; you do not have to hide it to cooperate.

Fictional patient: lower-left tooth pain since yesterday; worse when chewing; possible lost filling, not confirmed. Dentist proposes an examination, then discussion of treatment options; no treatment selected.
Give your report. Partner asks when and what makes it hurt. Answer with the case.
Partner asks you to open wider. Confirm what they mean and request a stopping signal.
Partner mentions a possible filling. Ask about findings, alternatives, and cost before deciding.
Change the role to a loose crown or a whitening inquiry. The type of concern and intended outcome should change.
Solo: read the dentist lines and create your replies, then describe the concern with the model hidden.
Possibilities:

“It hurts when I chew.” “Could we agree on a signal to pause?” “Could you explain the alternatives before I decide?” Check that the location, observation, uncertainty, and requested explanation are clear. Appointment changes belong to Chapter 82; this lesson focuses on the care conversation.

note: どの歯か、いつ痛むかを説明します。診察中にも、不快なことや確認したい治療の選択肢を伝えられます。
